reasons: Visual results were not checked in this review.
Some rules are checked by a test that reads the text of the print rule.
Class names used by the views were not all checked against this file.

terms.meaning: the stylesheet language that sets how a page looks
a named value, such as a colour, that rules can reuse
a block of styles used only when the page is printed
a page with all colour removed, as a monochrome printer produces

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Why each evidence state has several signals
sections.what: The header explains that each evidence state is shown by a text mark, a word, a border weight and a colour.

sections.name: :root
sections.title: Colour palette
sections.what: Names the colours used for the ink, the paper, the panels, the warnings and each of the three evidence states.
sections.why: Keeps the colours in one place so a change applies everywhere.

sections.name: body
sections.title: Base page typography and layout
sections.what: Sets the page font, the width of the content, and the header and heading sizes.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the usual page setup.

sections.name: .readonly
sections.title: Read-only badge and note
sections.what: Styles the small read-only label and the note beside it.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code, though the label marks the page as read only.

sections.name: nav button
sections.title: Navigation buttons
sections.what: Styles the buttons used to switch views and pick a case, including the active one.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .run-stamp
sections.title: Run stamp panel and bridge tables
sections.what: Styles the run stamp panel, the field rows and the bridge tables, including the net line, the inverted rows and the warning rows.
sections.why: The run stamp is the box that says which run produced the page. The bridge tables show the money walk.
sections.watch_out: The inverted row colour is the on-screen cue for scores where five is worse.

sections.name: .warning
sections.title: Warning box
sections.what: Styles a warning with a red left border and a pale red background.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the look of a warning.

sections.name: .evidence-toggle
sections.title: Evidence marks and their borders
sections.what: Styles each evidence toggle with its text mark, word and border: a solid line for grounded, a dashed line for declared prerequisite, and a double line for unsupported.
sections.why: The header says border weight is one of the channels that keeps the states apart without colour.
sections.watch_out: The print rules change these borders, so both must be kept in step.

sections.name: .edge-note, .cost-note
sections.title: Small notes under evidence and cost
sections.what: Styles the short notes that sit under an evidence mark or a cost, with a left border and a muted colour.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the visual grouping.

sections.name: .band-comparability
sections.title: Band notice in red
sections.what: Styles the band comparability notice with a strong red border and text so it stands out.
sections.why: The header says the notice must be loud on screen and louder in print, because the printed page is the one compared with past work.
sections.watch_out: This class is kept out of the structural hook list on purpose, because its class name carries meaning.

sections.name: tr.band-unmoved > td
sections.title: Rows of unmoved bands
sections.what: Styles the table rows for bands that did not change, with a pale red background and red text.
sections.why: The comments say the unmoved rows show the pattern: they are the two processes with no cited value parameters.
sections.watch_out: The styling relies on the class name set by the table code.

sections.name: tr.feature-absent > td:last-child
sections.title: Unmeasured feature row cell
sections.what: Styles the last cell of a feature row whose value was not measured, with a monospace font and centred text.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the layout.

sections.name: .dangling-note
sections.title: Dangling notes, confidence and assumption styles
sections.what: Styles the dangling citation notes, the evidence panels and cards, the confidence panels, the derivation table, the parameter basis boxes and the assumption list.
sections.why: The dangling note is a loud mark for a citation that points nowhere. The other rules give each confidence and assumption block its own look.
sections.watch_out: The dangling note is styled as loudly as the unsupported chip, so the two look alike by design.

sections.name: @media print
sections.title: Print rules
sections.what: Hides navigation when printing, keeps the run stamp and band notice with black borders, forces the evidence panels open, and keeps the evidence marks visible with black borders and a weight that survives greyscale.
sections.why: The header says a printed page with numbers but no depth tier cannot be checked, and that hiding the evidence toggle once removed all three evidence states from print.
sections.watch_out: The print rules use important flags, so a later rule that is not important will not override them.

summary: The stylesheet that sets the look of the viewer on screen and in print, so the evidence states stay distinct in every setting.
purpose: Shows each evidence state through several channels at once, keeps the band notice visible in print, and hides navigation when printing.
why: The header says colour alone fails in greyscale, in print, and for colour blind readers, so the states use text, border and colour together.
how: Sets the colours as named values, then sets the base layout and table styles. Styles the evidence marks by border and word. Styles the band notice, the unmoved rows and the confidence panels. The print section then overrides the colours, forces borders to black and hides navigation.
inputs: The class names that the components and views put on each element.
outputs: The layout and appearance of the page on screen and when printed.
risks: Print rules use important flags that override other rules. Hiding the evidence toggle would remove every evidence state from printed pages. Some rules are checked only by a test that reads the rule text.
debug: If an evidence state looks wrong, check the class names on that element. If something is missing from print, check the print section first.
